A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 20-page versions of the same TrendFact benchmark and FactISR framework. Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V4 reports original retrieval, verification, explanation-generation, ablation and efficiency results, plus gold-evidence experiments in Appendix I.

after.justification: V5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports influence-stratified results, ECS judge validation and influence-weight sensitivity findings.

M1.justification: FactISR retains dynamic evidence augmentation, influence-dependent iterative self-reflection, the same reflection-probability equation and the Figure 11 prompt. The expanded risk-based motivation does not establish a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use 7,643 Chinese claims from trending platforms and CHEF, five domains and 366,634 evidence entries. The added analyses examine existing coverage; the multilingual extension mentioned in v5 remains future work.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 3–7 and the gold-evidence comparisons, renumbered from Tables 10–11 to Tables 11–12. Human experts provide reference judgments for ECS validation, rather than an additional competing fact-checking method.

E3.justification: V5 adds evaluation across four influence groups, expert validation of over 100 randomly sampled instances, and ±20% influence-weight perturbations. These introduce supplementary protocols; the retained experiments' metrics and Appendix J inference budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 adds influence-stratified difficulty and error-exposure analysis in Figure 1, ECS judge validation in Appendix F, and HCPI weight sensitivity in Section 3.2. Existing component ablations, efficiency tests, resource-constrained evaluations, gold-evidence experiments and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V5's human-agreement percentages are point estimates, and its ±20% perturbation check reports sensitivity rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All existing numerical entries in Tables 3–7 and the gold-evidence tables remain identical. V5 adds ECS human-agreement rates of 95.68–100%, influence-group results including 7.4 billion versus 142.0 billion error-case views for low versus viral claims, and a finding of stable HCPI rankings under weight perturbations.

T1.justification: V5 completes HCPI's formal specification with an explicitly summed per-claim score and a zero case for remaining errors. V4's Appendix F leaves some prediction cases unspecified and presents the NEI contribution without an explicit summation. Existing penalty coefficients and ECS levels are retained; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: V5 makes empirical risk asymmetry under resource constraints a central contribution, adding claims about hotspot verification difficulty and roughly twentyfold social consequences. V4 primarily motivates the work through missing explanations, hotspot evaluation and Chinese benchmark coverage. The benchmark and FactISR contributions remain, but their central scientific framing changes substantially.

C2.justification: V5 specifies ECS as a system-level assessment rather than a user-facing trust signal, interprets lower BLEU/ROUGE through lexical-metric limitations, and attributes modest DEA gains to the evidence cap. It also explicitly identifies single-language coverage as an applicability limitation.

D1.justification: V5 newly states that influence weights derive from raw-data statistics and that FactISR avoids heavy few-shot reference prompting. Risk-score model identification becomes less specific, changing from GPT4.1 to GPT. Appendix J settings, supplied prompts and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds FrugalGPT, Vosoughi et al.'s news-diffusion study and Stable-RAG, while removing Damasceno et al. and WebThinker. It also adds positioning that distinguishes influence-triggered reflection from mechanisms triggered by model uncertainty; the broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list are extensively rewritten. V4's separate HPA and construction sections become a unified benchmark section, with reorganized metric exposition and expanded results interpretation. The title and author affiliations also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned to combine two new plots with an English-only rendering of the retained example, and Table 8 adds judge-validation results. Other figures retain their content, while several displays move and appendix tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: V5 improves evaluability through a more complete HCPI definition and initial checks of ECS judge agreement and HCPI weight sensitivity. These are limited gains: the new studies provide sparse procedural detail, and Figure 1's error-case views do not directly establish the claimed magnitude of social harm. The underlying method and existing benchmark results remain unchanged.
